record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.original_question: At low x and low Q^2, HERA data show that the scaling violations dF2/dlogQ^2 stabilize and then decrease, while the rise of F2 with decreasing x turns on only slowly. Can this scaling-violation behaviour and the slow onset of the low-x rise of F2 be understood simultaneously within a single description of the transition from soft to hard physics?

evidence.quote: The question is whether this scaling violation behaviour and the slow onset of the rise of F2 with decreasing x can be simultaneously understood.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider deep inelastic electron-proton scattering and the proton structure function $F_2(x,Q^2)$, where $x$ is the Bjorken scaling variable and $Q^2$ is the negative squared four-momentum transfer. In the kinematic region of small $x$ and small $Q^2$ (the transition region between the soft, Regge/hadron-like regime and the hard, perturbative-QCD regime), experimental measurements display two qualitative features:

1. The logarithmic scaling violations $\partial F_2/\partial \log Q^2$, plotted as a function of $x$ at fixed $Q^2$, first grow with decreasing $Q^2$ but then stabilize and ultimately decrease as $Q^2$ becomes small.
2. The rise of $F_2$ as $x$ decreases (at fixed small $Q^2$) sets in only slowly, becoming progressively weaker as $Q^2$ is lowered toward the photoproduction limit.

Question: Construct a single theoretical description of the transition from soft (non-perturbative, Regge-dominated) to hard (perturbative QCD) physics that simultaneously and quantitatively accounts for both phenomena above — namely, the observed $Q^2$-dependent behaviour of the scaling violations $\partial F_2/\partial \log Q^2$ at low $x$ and low $Q^2$, and the slow onset of the low-$x$ rise of $F_2$ in the same regime — within one consistent framework valid across the soft-to-hard transition.
artifact.category_tag: Deep inelastic scattering at low x
artifact.status_search_result: Several phenomenological frameworks proposed since the late 1990s (dipole models such as Golec-Biernat–Wüsthoff and its CGC/saturation extensions, two-Pomeron and tensor-Pomeron Regge models, and combined soft+hard QCD-evolution fits) successfully describe both the stabilization/decrease of dF2/dlogQ^2 and the slow onset of the low-x rise of F2 in the transition region. There is, however, no unique or universally accepted "first-principles" description; the question of a single unified soft-to-hard framework remains an active area of phenomenology rather than a fully settled theoretical result.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the proton structure function F2 at low x and low Q2 at HERA
status_evidence.snippet: At low Q2 the rise of F2 at low x can be described by Regge theory with a constant logarithmic slope; the Q2 dependence is stronger than at higher Q2.
status_evidence.claim: Phenomenological descriptions of the transition region exist and partially capture the observed behaviour.

status_evidence.title: Two-tensor-Pomeron model for soft-to-hard transition
status_evidence.snippet: A soft tensor Pomeron together with a hard tensor Pomeron and subleading Reggeons gives a good description of photon-proton cross sections from low to high Q^2.
status_evidence.claim: Two-component (soft+hard) Pomeron models provide a unified description across the transition.

status_evidence.title: Implications of Scaling Violations of F2 at HERA for Perturbative QCD
status_evidence.snippet: DGLAP evolution combined with appropriate input distributions describes scaling violations down to low Q^2, but the very low Q^2 region requires non-perturbative input.
status_evidence.claim: Perturbative QCD alone is insufficient at the lowest Q^2; combined frameworks are needed.
